name: Latvia
summary: A carmine red field with a narrow white horizontal stripe. Based on a 13th-century account, it was designed in 1917, banned under Soviet rule, and restored in 1990.
origin: The Livonian Rhymed Chronicle of the late 13th century describes a red banner with a white stripe carried by Latgalian tribesmen. A legend says a wounded chieftain was wrapped in a white sheet that was stained with his blood except where he lay.
The artist Ansis Cīrulis designed the modern flag in 1917; it was adopted by the Republic of Latvia in 1921. Banned after the Soviet occupation of 1940, it was restored on 27 February 1990.

colors.name: Carmine red
colors.meaning: Commonly read as the blood shed for freedom; the dark shade is sometimes called 'Latvian red'.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Commonly read as honesty and right; in the legend, the sheet.

history.label: Latvian SSR
history.note: Red with white and blue waves.

facts: Austria's flag also has red-white-red bands, but bright red and equal widths.
The 13th-century chronicle makes it one of the oldest flag designs on record.
clues: A dark carmine red flag with a narrow white horizontal stripe.
A legend says it shows a chieftain's blood-stained sheet.
A 13th-century chronicle describes a banner like it.
